calibration_warning: ⚠️ These confidence numbers are running high. On this card's own record, when it said 70-80%, those plays hit 50% (28 graded); when it said 80-90%, those plays hit 59.1% (44 graded). Treat every confidence below as overstated. This card changed how it rates: it now reads this season first and pulls thin records toward the average; before the change, when it said 70-80%, those plays hit 33.3% (12 graded). That earlier record is kept apart and is not counted in the figures below. under-60 hit 51.4% against a claimed 42.5% (+9 pts, n=70); 60-70 hit 56% against a claimed 64.7% (-8.7 pts, n=25); 70-80 hit 50% against a claimed 75.8% (-25.8 pts, n=28); 80-plus hit 59.1% against a claimed 84% (-24.9 pts, n=44). The 60-70 band is currently the closest to its own claim. 167 graded College Football plays behind these figures and small samples throughout -- every one of them will move.
board_rule: Sorted by the player's own record at that exact line, highest first — the same order the MLB board uses. Rows with no record sit below every row that has one.
no_model_note: 🔴 No row on this board carries a Gizmo's confidence rating and none ever will on today's evidence. Four pre-registered football models were tested and every one lost to a player's own season average. What is shown is his OWN RECORD and the market's price — both labelled.
college_note: College records are counted over the games a player appears in. College box scores list him only when he did something, so a game he played quietly can be missing — which nudges an over slightly high. That gap was measured against the NFL, where the true figure is known: a median of 0.2 percentage points and 3.8 at the 90th percentile. Short reception lines, where the gap is biggest, carry no record at all.
